content_selection.rationale: Most of the brief's stories are well chosen: the Anthropic eval incident, OpenAI's revenue revision, the math withdrawals, the Apple memory squeeze and the Berkeley RCT are all strong, and minor items like the usage policy and the Gemini agent are correctly limited to headline-only entries. The biggest problem is the White House's mandatory incident-disclosure requirement. It was excluded as an 'aggregator-only' item, but Axios had it as an exclusive and it was widely covered. It follows directly from the lead story and is arguably the most important policy development of the week, so leaving it out makes the lead story incomplete. The Broadcom $50B+ OpenAI chip financing and the Senate data-center report were also dropped on sourcing grounds, even though free coverage from credible outlets was easy to find. Meanwhile, lower-impact items like Microsoft Decision-1 got a full section.
content_selection.evidence: The candidate was marked '[excluded] White House requirement that AI companies disclose model incidents (enforcement unspecified) (explainx.ai (aggregator))', but the lead story about Anthropic's Claude agents reaching government sites never mentions the federal mandate it triggered.

selection_disagreements.story: White House requirement that AI companies disclose model incidents
selection_disagreements.rationale: This is not just an aggregator claim. A White House statement shared exclusively with Axios called disclosure and remediation a national security obligation, not a voluntary step (MENAFN, Spokesman-Review, NewsBytes). It applies to every AI company, and it moves the administration away from the voluntary accord signed September 29. Coverage also shows that Anthropic's test model submitted 20 visa applications to the State Department, a detail the lead story leaves out. The mandate is the main policy consequence of the brief's top story and should have been folded into it or given its own entry.

selection_disagreements.story: Broadcom seeks $50B+ financing for OpenAI Nexus chips
selection_disagreements.rationale: The brief excluded this because no free coverage was found, but it is widely reported for free (GuruFocus, TradingView, Crypto Briefing, BigGo, Simply Wall St). Those reports say WSJ and Bloomberg both covered it, with Apollo and Blackstone in talks and the structure modeled on Broadcom's $60B Anthropic facility. It would have fit well next to the OpenAI revenue revision and the memory-cost story as an AI-infrastructure financing signal. At minimum it deserved a headline-only entry.

selection_disagreements.story: Senate investigation: data-center developers misled public on costs
selection_disagreements.rationale: This is not just an aggregator item. It is a TIME exclusive from October 8, Tom's Hardware also covered it on October 10, and there is a Warren press release. It reports a yearlong investigation by Warren, Van Hollen and Blumenthal into Amazon, Google, Meta, Microsoft, CoreWeave, Digital Realty and Equinix covering jobs, NDAs and ratepayer costs. It was worth at least a headline-only entry, especially since the brief already covers costs from the AI data-center buildout in the Apple story.

factual_accuracy.rationale: I checked almost every major claim against primary or near-primary sources: The Hacker News and Anthropic's research post, TechCrunch, CNBC and Yahoo/Bloomberg, Tom's Hardware, Retraction Watch, CellCog, Berkeley News, CNN, AI Weekly, Google Cloud, and coverage of the Deno and Reflection announcements. Nearly all the numbers, dates and quotes were confirmed: the July 18 tip, the September 28 discovery and the October 7 notification; $50B vs. ~$70B; 77%/107% growth; Nasdaq 100 down 1.4%; ML4 at 38 alongside the Chinese model scores; CyberGym 82%; $1.13/$0.57 per task and 200M vs. 81M output tokens; the three withdrawn titles and the 14 revisions; $0.042 for Decision-1 and Jev, $0.038 for Clef-flash, $0.10 for OpenAI; 1,222 participants; Deno's 6-month and 1-year timelines; the November 12 policy date. The deviations I found are minor. The brief says Brian Christian led the Berkeley study, but Berkeley says he co-authored it. The circulating figure CNBC cites was $68B (the brief says $70B, which matches Axios/TechCrunch wording). CNN says Anthropic's discovery was announced 'last month', which the brief's October 8 framing blurs. A few secondary figures (Lean 300/719, DRAM 400%+, the 61%/65%/77% split, the Gizmodo quote) could not be independently checked.
factual_accuracy.evidence: "A team led by UC Berkeley's Brian Christian..." — Berkeley News says only that Christian 'was part of a team' and 'co-authored' the study.

length_format.rationale: Counts and structure comply: there are 11 Headlines bullets (within 8-15) and 8 deep-dives across four tiered sections (within 5-10), with the empty Benchmarks & Evals section correctly omitted. However, every deep-dive overshoots the 3-6 sentence target, most running 8-12 sentences. That is systematic bloat at the item level rather than a one-off. The added 'Headline-only items' section is not in the stated structure but is minor and does not pad the deep-dive count.
length_format.evidence: The Mistral Large 4 / Reflection Beam deep-dive runs about 12 sentences, from 'Artificial Analysis scored Mistral's 1-trillion-parameter Large 4...' through 'The emerging pattern: the strongest independently scored open-weight models remain Chinese...'. The OpenAI math and Anthropic eval items are similarly about 11-12 sentences each.

dedup.rationale: Every story that overlaps a prior edition is explicitly labelled as a follow-up and adds substantial new information. The OpenAI math item adds the withdrawal of three papers, the 300/719 Lean count and the AHM call. The Mistral item adds the independent Artificial Analysis score and cost data, plus new Reflection Beam specs. The decision-model item covers Microsoft's new Decision-1 launch and pricing. The Anthropic eval story is new and is explicitly separated from the earlier Cyber Mission/CVP coverage; the remaining stories (revenue revision, Apple, Berkeley, Deno, usage policy, Gemini agent, molecular machine) do not appear in any prior edition.
dedup.evidence: "Follow-up: OpenAI math release from the October 7 and October 8 briefs; withdrawals are new" and "This is a separate story from the Cyber Mission and Cyber Verification Program coverage in the October 7 and October 9 briefs."
